thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and increased latency observed for Hosted API and several Dedicated pools in ap-southeast-2. Error surface shows STS/KMS auth failures from upstream AWS region APIs. Automated paging triggered.

mike (oncall-sre): I’m on it. seeing a spike in 503s from the auth-proxy layer and a bunch of 504s from the model-serving gateways.

sara (infra): Confirmed. CloudTrail shows STS:AssumeRole errors and KMS decrypt timeouts for requests backing token validation. AWS status page (ap-southeast-2) reports "degraded" for STS and KMS.

juan (eng-runtime): Logs from runtime: `ERROR kv_cache: auth refresh failed, upstream 502 STS` repeated across many hosts. Sequence lengths unaffected, but tail latencies spike 3-4x.

lina (support): We have multiple customers reporting increased latencies and some 5xxs for generation calls. CS triage queue has a few high-severity tickets.

mike (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Short-circuit auth calls using cached tokens for known long-lived sessions 2) Route new requests to other regions as fallback for Hosted where policy allows 3) For Dedicated, spin up cross-region fallback nodes if customer permits.

jess (product): Heads-up: some enterprise customers may have region restrictions. need to surface opt-in for cross-region failover in support responses.

juan (eng-runtime): Working on a patch: allow token TTL override in auth middleware. Pushing a canary to low-traffic hosts.

mike (oncall-sre): Command I’m running on proxy nodes to enable caching (temp):
```
# enable short-term token cache
kubectl exec -n redwood proxy-ctrl -- /bin/sh -c "export RW_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL=300 && pkill -HUP proxy"
```

sara (infra): Also increasing regional routing weight to us-east-1 for Hosted API by 20% to relieve ap-southeast-2. Doing gradual shift to avoid amplification.

incident-bot: Paging escalation: yana (oncall-sre-lead) in 12m unless resolved.

lina (support): Drafting customer comms: short status note + recommendation to retry and mention we’re routing traffic. Will ping affected accounts who explicitly restrict region failover.

juan (eng-runtime): Canary results after 3m: token cache cut auth-related errors by ~60% on canary hosts, latency improved ~40ms median. Rolling to additional hosts.

mike (oncall-sre): For Dedicated pools: starting live migration of a small subset to eu-west-1 dedicated nodes where policies allow. Will coordinate with account owners.

sara (infra): Note: KMS decrypt failures also causing metrics ingestion errors into our observability pipeline; some dashboards show delayed points. Don’t rely solely on one view for impact.

juan (eng-runtime): Stack snippet we applied to bypass redundant STS calls: 
```
if (cachedCreds.valid()) return cachedCreds;
// else fallback to local signing with cached ephemeral creds
```

lina (support): CC’ing affected enterprise contacts now. Template: "We're seeing an AWS regional auth degradation impacting latency and occasional 5xxs. We've applied token-caching mitigations and are routing traffic to alternative regions; some customers may see a small change in region. We'll follow up when AWS reports resolution."

mike (oncall-sre): Quick test for customers who reported 5xx: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.hosted/v1/generate` — observed header returned 503 with upstream STS error in body. After cache enabled, same call returned 200 for canary hosts.

jess (product): Are billing/usage metrics affected? need to avoid false overage alerts for customers during reroutes.

sara (infra): Observability delayed but raw request counters look accurate. I'll tag the affected metric series as "inc_ap_southeast_2_sts" so billing queries filter it out for now.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation in progress. Current severity: P2 -> tracking under incident-2112500000. Next update in 15m or on major change.

mike (oncall-sre): Handoff note for next oncall (yana): applied token-cache TTL=300, routing shift +20% to us-east-1, initiated cross-region Dedicated migration on opt-in tenants, canary rollout passed. Remaining work: monitor AWS status, revert temp TTL on healthy day, prepare postmortem on dependency risk.

juan (eng-runtime): Opening a follow-up PR to persist safe token caching and add circuit-breaker on STS calls. PR will include telemetry for cache hit ratio and auth error classes.

lina (support): Customer impact summary for ops: ~8% of requests in ap-southeast-2 returned 5xx during peak, primarily auth failures. Top affected customers contacted, CS escalations created.

jess (product): Please include a short blurb in the weekly incident digest: "Third-party AWS auth/KMS degradation caused elevated latency and 5xxs; temporary mitigations applied; longer-term work to reduce dependency blast radius."

mike (oncall-sre): AWS status just updated: STS recovered in ap-southeast-2 but KMS still intermittent. Rolling back routing shift slowly.

sara (infra): Observability backlog starting to flush. Dashboards coming back to normal. Recommend keeping token-cache for 24h and then evaluate.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to P3. Close when postmortem created and customer comms sent. :white_check_mark:

mike (oncall-sre): Closing handoff: passing to yana for postmortem and blameless review. Thanks all.

lina (support): Sent final customer updates with mitigation summary and next steps.

juan (eng-runtime): Adding runbook entry for token-cache toggle and cross-region fallback playbook.

jess (product): Filing follow-up: request product review of region-fallback UX and enterprise opt-in language.

mike (oncall-sre): End of thread.
